texts.preamble: Suresh Agarwal @ Suresh Kumar Agarwal vs Unknown on 26 June, 2020 Author: Sanjib Banerjee Bench: Sanjib Banerjee 1 26.06.2020 rc Crm 4454 of 2020 with Cran 2608 of 2020 (Via Video Conference) In Re: - An application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in connection with Posta Police Station Case No. 38 of 2020 dated 12.03.2020 under Sections 120/269/273 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. And In the matter of: Suresh Agarwal @ Suresh Kumar Agarwal ....Petitioner. Mr. Shiladitya Banerjee ...for the Petitioner.
texts.facts: The petitioner undertakes to affirm and stamp the petition as per the Rules within 48 hours of resumption of normal functioning of the court. The petition is taken up through video conference on the basis of such undertaking. The petitioner claims that certain samples were drawn from the petitioner's shop and the goods were apparently seized but left in the custody of the petitioner. A subsequent complaint has been lodged on the allegation that some of the samples reveal sub- standard goods. The petitioner says that sub-standard goods cannot be understood to imply spurious goods as the expressions "sub- standard" and "spurious" have been defined in the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The State says that what was discovered was that harmful substance was being sold and such substance was not fit for human consumption.
